title: Rav Huna son of Rav Nachman
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Hyman identifies his father Rav Nachman as the well-known Rav Nachman without further designation, as stated explicitly in Chullin 49b: “Rava said: I heard two things from Rav Nachman: chimtzei and bar chimtzei; one seals [a perforation] and one does not seal, and I do not know which of them. Rav Huna bar Chinena and Rav Huna son of Rav Nachman said: Bar chimtza seals; chimtza does not seal. Rav Tavut said: And your mnemonic is: the power of the son is greater than the power of the father.” (Although the Gemara’s intent is the difference between chimtza and bar chimtza — that bar chimtza seals — Hyman suggests we can also say that the meaning is that the father did not explain and the son did.) He and his colleague Rav Huna bar Chinena lived in the town of Sikhra near Mechoza, and both disagreed with Rava, as cited in Avodah Zarah 57b: Rava permitted wine that a gentile had stirred, to be sold to a gentile, and Rav Huna bar Chinena and Rav Huna son of Rav Nachman forbade it; when he came to Mechoza and asked Rava, Rava then retracted. In Bekhorot 54b he challenges Rava’s words; he is likewise mentioned in Eruvin 42b, according to Dikdukei Soferim; in the Gemara it reads Rav Huna son of Rav Natan.

Hyman concludes from this that he was like Rava’s colleague. In Horayot 12b it is cited: Rav Papa sat and was in doubt; Huna son of Rav Nachman said to Rav Papa, “We have learned it”; (Rav Papa) rose, kissed him on his head and gave him his daughter. He considers it beyond any doubt that this is not Rav Huna son of Rav Nachman: (1) because in Bava Metzia they called him “Rav” Huna, not Huna; (2) could one who was Rava’s colleague be younger than Rav Papa, who was Rava’s student? Hyman instead proposes Huna Mar son of Rav Nechemyah, who was in Rav Ashi’s academy, as explained in his entry; it was written בדר״נ, and from this came “son of Rav Nachman.”

notes.text: Saved Davidson Chullin49b explains חימצא/barחימצא as two fats of the abomasum, one sealing a perforation; סתים means seals, not is closed. Hyman’s son/father pun and his genealogy argument are retained as interpretations. Supplied ר״ג הגודע is read ר״נ הנודע by full heading and connected witness. The age argument is a rhetorical question, not reversed terms; the kinship narrative alone is not independent proof of the relative ages. בב״מ remains BavaMetzia as supplied, without asserting its proposed בכ״מ correction.

The consulted Horayot 12b narrative has Papa giving Huna his daughter; this direction alone does not prove Hyman’s relative-age conclusion. The abomasum fats seal a perforation, preserving the son/father pun. Hyman’s well-known Nachman equation and beyond-any-doubt rejection remain attributed, as does the proposed Huna Mar reconstruction. The rhetorical question is not reversed terms, and supplied Bava Metzia is not silently changed to everywhere.
